key_insight: ETCH-X combines composable datasets with a modular two-stage fitting pipeline to achieve both global robustness (to clothing, occlusion, noise, partial scans) and local expressiveness (hands, face) when aligning parametric body models to clothed 3D point clouds.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between capturing fine local detail and maintaining robust global alignment for fitting SMPL/SMPL‑X style models to real-world, clothed human scans that exhibit varied clothing, poses, noise, and missing regions.
method: Composable-dataset strategy: aggregate and augment heterogeneous real and synthetic datasets (targeted clothing, poses, occlusions) to cover diverse real-world variability.
Two-stage fitting pipeline: (a) robust global alignment to noisy/partial point clouds, (b) local expressive refinement modules specialized for hands, face, and fine surface detail.
Clothing- and occlusion-aware objectives and curriculum-style training to separate body shape from clothing and stabilize fitting across domains.
impact: Makes parametric body fitting more reliable on in-the-wild scans and consumer sensors, reducing manual cleanup and improving downstream tasks (animation, retargeting, texturing) by providing stable, detail-preserving body estimates.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset composition → robust global fit → local expressive refinement (annotated modules and data flow).
Before/after examples: raw clothed point cloud vs fitted parametric model with zoom-ins on hands and face detail.
Dataset collage: thumbnails showing combined real/synthetic/augmented samples (different clothing, poses, occlusions).
Robustness chart: bar/line plot comparing performance under noise, partial views, and clothing complexity across baselines and ETCH-X.
paper_title: ETCH-X: Robustify Expressive Body Fitting to Clothed Humans with Composable Datasets
paper_authors: Xiaoben Li, Jingyi Wu, Zeyu Cai, Yu Siyuan, Boqian Li
